findings.finding: audited_at` timestamps are compared as raw strings. Lexicographic comparison is only correct if every timestamp uses the identical format and UTC offset. If the digest ever contains mixed offsets (e.g. `2026-09-26T12:00:00+02:00` vs `2026-09-26T11:30:00+00:00` — the earlier instant sorts "newer"), or different precision/format (`2026-09-26 10:00` vs ISO-T), the wrong block is chosen and a genuine current FAIL is silently suppressed or a stale one replayed — the exact bug this change exists to fix.
findings.suggestion: Parse timestamps (e.g. `datetime.fromisoformat`, falling back to the empty-string-oldest rule on parse failure) and compare the parsed instants; keep the tie-break on the earlier block.

findings.finding: The `audited_at` regex is applied to every stripped line after a header, and the "first wins" guard (`not blocks[-1][2]`) only protects against a second `audited_at:` in the same block. A line inside a FAIL evidence list that happens to read `- audited_at: <something>` would be captured as the block's timestamp. Low likelihood, but the parse is unscoped.
findings.suggestion: Only accept `audited_at` lines while not inside an `open FAILs:` section, mirroring `_collect_tier1_fails`'s section tracking.

findings.finding: The code compares `audited_at` as text. Valid timestamps with different UTC offsets can sort in the wrong order: `2026-09-26T12:00:00+02:00` is earlier than `2026-09-26T11:00:00+00:00`, but this comparison selects the former. That can keep reporting a superseded FAIL.
findings.suggestion: Parse timestamps as timezone-aware datetimes and compare their instants. Add a regression test using two valid offsets.
